nodes.title: The elliptic admissible-cover specialization
nodes.statement: For finite G and S over Z[1/|G|], restrict the imported admissible (g,n)-cover stack to (1,1), identifying a stable one-pointed genus-one target with a 1-generalized elliptic curve E/S. Write A_G for this stack and A_G^0 for its smooth-target open. Retain the imported finite quotient map C→E, connected prestable source, G-torsor off the origin and nodes, tame cyclic inertia, and balanced charts x=ξ^e at a marking and (x,y)=(ξ^r,η^r), ξη=a, xy=a^r at a node. nodes.title: The reduced ramification divisor
nodes.statement: For an elliptic admissible cover π:C→E over S, let Δ(H) be the smooth fixed locus C_sm^H with all fixed loci C_sm^K for strictly larger cyclic K removed. Define R_π as the disjoint union of Δ(H) over nontrivial cyclic H≤G, with the induced fixed-locus scheme structures. It is an effective Cartier divisor finite étale over S, with geometrically reduced fibres; it is reduced as a scheme if S is reduced. The converse holds when R_π→S is surjective, in particular for e≥2 on a nonempty connected base. On a connected base the origin ramification index e is constant; if e≥2, R_π has degree |G|/e and is the fibrewise reduced origin fibre. If e=1, R_π is empty and the full marking is the whole étale origin fibre.
hypotheses: G finite; all bases over Z[1/|G|]; additional characteristic-zero or generation assumptions are stated in the target.
proofSteps: Use the tame smooth local chart to identify each fixed locus with a section after an étale cover.
Separate loci with different stabilizer subgroups; these are disjoint in the smooth locus.
Descend their union and the Cartier property, and count the geometric fibre G/H.
acceptance: Every unramified connected cover has R_π=∅, even though π^{-1}(O) has |G| points.
For S3 inertia of order 3, R_π has degree 2.
For the chart x=ξ^e, e≥2, R_π is ξ=0 with multiplicity one, not the different divisor of multiplicity e−1.

nodes.title: Monodromy of the ramification divisor
nodes.statement: Assume S connected and π as above with e≥2. For a geometric ramified point x with inertia H, all connected components of R_π are isomorphic finite étale Galois covers of S. Their deck groups embed in N_G(H)/H. If S is regular integral and contains a primitive e-th root of unity, these groups embed in C_G(H)/H. For a connected component X of A_G over Z[1/|G|,ζ_e], the same assertion holds for the universal ramification divisor, by finite étale monodromy and descent of the inertia character.
hypotheses: G finite; all bases over Z[1/|G|]; additional characteristic-zero or generation assumptions are stated in the target.
proofSteps: The G-action commutes with finite étale monodromy and is transitive on the whole geometric fibre G/H.
An equivariant permutation is determined by its value at H; its stabilizer condition gives the normalizer quotient.
The faithful inertia character, constant over a regular integral base containing ζ_e, forces centralization.

For the universal stack, the fixed-subgroup loci of the finite étale ramification divisor are open and closed. On each connected component the faithful inertia character takes constant values in the constant group μ_e. Monodromy preserves that character, so its normalizer image centralizes H. Descend this character calculation through an atlas; a connected atlas alone need not preserve connected finite covers.
acceptance: The centralizer quotient, not the normalizer quotient, supplies d_X in the characteristic-zero congruence.
For odd dihedral G and full rotation inertia, the centralizer quotient has order 1.

nodes.title: The Higman invariant
nodes.statement: Fix ζ_n on a Z[1/|G|]-base, with every inertia order e dividing n. At a point x over O the faithful action on its cotangent line is χ_x:H→μ_e. Define Hig_ζ(π) in ConjClasses(G) as the class of the unique c in H with χ_x(c)=ζ_n^(n/e). Set e=1 and c=1 in the unramified case. This is independent of the point and compatible with base change and isomorphisms. With right G-actions and a positively oriented punctured-torus basis (a,b), the positive peripheral loop is [b,a], for [x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}.
hypotheses: G finite; all bases over Z[1/|G|]; additional characteristic-zero or generation assumptions are stated in the target.
proofSteps: Use the tame local chart to prove χ_x faithful.
Changing x conjugates the generator, and étale-local charts give base-change compatibility.
Compare the chosen root-of-unity generator with the oriented complex peripheral loop.
acceptance: For every abelian G, all elliptic G-covers have Higman class 1, since every commutator is 1.
For a generating pair of S3 consisting of two distinct transpositions, the Higman class is the class of 3-cycles and e=3.
Replacing ζ_e by its inverse inverts the inertia generator; no equality of a class with its inverse is assumed in a general finite group.

nodes.title: Open and closed Higman strata
nodes.statement: The index e and Hig_ζ are locally constant on A_G and on its smooth locus. Hence, after adjoining the requisite roots, each fixed conjugacy class gives an open and closed substack, and the disjoint union of these substacks is the whole moduli stack. The decomposition descends through the central rigidification and agrees on coarse spaces.

nodes.title: The sheaf of G-structures
nodes.statement: On the étale site of the elliptic moduli stack over Z[1/|G|], T_G is the sheafification of the presheaf assigning to E/S the isomorphism classes of right G-torsors over E\O with geometrically connected fibres over S. A G-structure is a section of this sheaf; M(G) is its associated stack over M(1). Over a separably closed field these sections are actual torsor classes. For center-free G the presheaf is already a sheaf. For general bases and nontrivial center, sheaf sections are not identified with global torsors without descent data.

nodes.title: Geometry of the finite étale level stack
nodes.statement: M(G)→M(1) is representable finite étale over Z[1/|G|]. M(G) is smooth separated Deligne–Mumford. Its coarse scheme is normal affine, finite over the affine j-line, smooth of relative dimension one over Z[1/|G|], and étale away from j=0,1728. Formation of this coarse scheme commutes with a base change to a regular Noetherian base, or to an arbitrary base when 6 divides |G|. A non-two-generated G gives the empty stack.

proofSteps: Use the locally constant finite connected-torsor sheaf to obtain the representable finite étale morphism.
Use the existing coarse j-line and tame or regular-base coarse comparison, with the stated base-change hypotheses.
Identify the geometric fibre by exterior epimorphisms; its emptiness is the generation obstruction.
acceptance: G=1 gives the level-one stack and the same coarse j-line.

nodes.title: Elliptic monodromy and branch cycles
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, use a complex comparison and a positively oriented basis of F2=π1(E\O) to identify the geometric fibre of M(G) with Epi^ext(F2,G). The connected components are Out^+(F2)-orbits. On exterior pairs the branch operators are γ0(a,b)=(ab^{-1},a), γ1728(a,b)=(b^{-1},a), γ∞(a,b)=(a,ab), and γ−I(a,b)=(a^{-1},b^{-1}). The generic coarse fibre is the quotient by γ−I, and fibres at 0,1728,∞ are respectively quotients by γ0, γ1728, and the subgroup generated by γ−I and γ∞. Stack monodromy uses π1(M(1)^an), not π1 of the coarse affine line.
hypotheses: G finite; all bases over Z[1/|G|]; additional characteristic-zero or generation assumptions are stated in the target.
proofSteps: Import C.0/moduli-monodromy for the analytic ordered moduli stack. The additional Nielsen identification for the punctured torus, stack Riemann existence and compatible orientation remain the exact G-MAPPING contract.
Apply the existing exterior-epimorphism fibre description to the elliptic universal family.
Compute the four words and the stabilizer quotients, distinguishing stack and coarse fibres.
Transport through characteristic-zero algebraically closed base extension.
acceptance: For G=1 every fibre has one element and every branch operator acts trivially.
For G=C2, the three nonzero pairs form one degree-three coarse component; the inversion acts trivially.
The generic stack fibre can have twice the size of the coarse fibre when γ−I has no fixed point on the orbit; neither size may replace the other.

The odd-dihedral obstruction example: Compute the dihedral generating pairs and their commutators directly.
The Higman and Nielsen congruences: If c=1, the claimed modulus is 1 and the conclusion is immediate; otherwise the inertia order is at least 2.

nodes.title: The normal-subgroup-free obstruction bound
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be prime, G finite nonabelian and c∈G, with r=ν_ℓ(|c|) and r+s=ν_ℓ(|G|). Assume G has no proper normal subgroup whose order is divisible by ℓ. If k=ν_ℓ(m′_c)>0, then G contains C_{ℓ^k}×C_{ℓ^k}, hence 2k≤r+s. Also ν_ℓ(d′_c)≤s. Consequently ν_ℓ(m′_c)≤⌊(r+s)/2⌋. This is the j=0 case only; it does not assert the printed general-j bound.
hypotheses: Finite nonabelian G; ℓ prime; valuation and normal-subgroup hypotheses exactly as stated.
proofSteps: Choose a cusp cyclic stabilizer containing z of order ℓ^k. Because |A| divides |u||Z(G)| and Z(G) is a proper normal ℓ-free subgroup, ℓ^k divides |u|.
Put U=⟨u⟩ and U_h=⟨h^{-1}uh⟩. Their intersection is normalized by h (equal orders of subgroups in a cyclic group) and by u, hence is a proper normal ℓ-free subgroup.
The cyclic groups ⟨z⟩∩U and ⟨z⟩∩U_h cannot both have nontrivial ℓ-parts: their unique subgroups of order ℓ would coincide inside ⟨z⟩ and lie in U∩U_h. Choose the one with trivial intersection.

Since z centralizes U and U_h, its product with the chosen cyclic subgroup of order ℓ^k is C_{ℓ^k}². Lagrange gives 2k≤r+s. The inequality ν_ℓ(d′_c)≤s follows from |c|d′_c≤|G|. General j needs a repaired intersection estimate and is recorded as G-GENERAL-J.
acceptance: The absence of ℓ-divisible proper normal subgroups is essential; D10 at ℓ=5 violates it and has m′=5.
For r=1,s=0 the inequality forces k=0.

nodes.title: Trace strata of SL2-covers
nodes.statement: For a prime power q and an SL2(F_q)-cover over Qbar, fix the compatible roots exp(2πi/n) through a chosen embedding in C. Define its trace invariant t as tr(c), where c is its Higman representative in SL2(F_q). Conjugacy invariance makes it independent of the ramification point. The t-strata are unions of Higman strata and are open and closed. The invariant descends through central rigidification and GL2(F_q)-conjugation. The root convention is part of the definition; arbitrary coprime powers of c need not preserve its trace.
hypotheses: Commutative coefficient rings for integral trace identities; finite fields for trace fibres; q restrictions exactly as stated.
proofSteps: Apply matrix trace to a Higman representative with the fixed root convention.
Use trace invariance under conjugation and the local constancy of Higman classes.
Descend along the central rigidification and the diagonal outer action.
acceptance: A noncentral matrix −[[1,1],[0,1]] in odd characteristic has trace −2 and order 2p.
Trace −2 does not force the matrix to equal −I.
In characteristic 2 the labels 2 and −2 coincide, so they cannot define disjoint strata.

nodes.title: Admissible trace classes
nodes.statement: Call a conjugacy class, or trace, q-admissible if it occurs as the commutator class, or trace, of a generating pair of SL2(F_q). For G=SL2(F_q), a trace t occurs as the commutator of a generating pair precisely as follows: all t≠2 for q=2,4,8 or q≥13; all t other than 1,2 for q=3,9,11; all t other than 0,2,4 for q=5; all t other than 0,1,2 for q=7. For t≠±2 there is one SL2-conjugacy class of trace t. When q is odd and −2 is admissible there are two admissible noncentral classes of trace −2, interchanged by a nonsquare-determinant GL2-conjugation. The central class of −I is excluded from these two classes.

Separate central and noncentral unipotent conjugacy classes.
Check the exceptional small fields by exhaustive exact enumeration, recording q and the admitted set; do not infer them from a generic q formula.
acceptance: For q=5 the admissible traces are 1 and 3=−2.
For q=3, −2=1 is excluded.
The two noncentral −2 classes are distinguished before passing to the GL2-induced outer quotient.

nodes.statement: For a∈F_q define n_q(a) to be the order of any noncentral element of SL2(F_q) of trace a. For q even and a=0 it is 2. For q odd, n_q(2)=p and n_q(−2)=2p. nodes.title: The rank-two SL2 character scheme
nodes.statement: For every commutative ring R, take the existing affine scheme SL2_R×SL2_R with diagonal GL2_R-conjugation. Its affine invariant quotient is the rank-two SL2 character scheme. The map (A,B)↦(tr A,tr B,tr AB) induces an isomorphism of invariant coordinate algebras R[x,y,z]≅O(SL2²)^GL2, and hence an isomorphism of the quotient with A³_R, compatible with every ring base change. Invariants here mean the group-scheme coaction, not invariance under only the finite group of R-valued points.
hypotheses: Commutative coefficient rings for integral trace identities; finite fields for trace fibres; q restrictions exactly as stated.
proofSteps: Request the exact integral n=2 matrix-invariant generation, arbitrary-base-change, and determinant-one restriction statements Q-INVARIANTS from LP.3. These do not follow from the mere existence of reductive invariants.
Reduce words in two determinant-one 2×2 matrices by Cayley–Hamilton to the three traces.
Prove algebraic independence on a universal three-parameter family, then use the requested integral base-change theorem.
acceptance: For (I,I) the coordinates are (2,2,2), with values reduced in R.
After reduction Z→F2 the same polynomial algebra is obtained; dividing by 2 in the proof is invalid.
Reducible pairs with identical semisimplification can have equal coordinates without being conjugate; the quotient does not classify all actual orbits.

Every Aut^+(F2)-orbit O on X_t*(q) has size divisible by n/gcd(n,4m/n) for odd q and by n/gcd(n,m/n) for even q. These are the moduli after the possible factor-two loss from the component congruence when quotienting by D(q,G). For prime p≥3 and t=−2, every such orbit has size divisible by p. Consequently every orbit of the larger full Markoff move group on the punctured prime-field Markoff surface also has size divisible by p. More generally for t≠±2 and odd ℓ with r=ν_ℓ(n_q(t)),r+s=ν_ℓ(q³−q), every such orbit has size divisible by ℓ^max(r−s,0).
hypotheses: q=p^f≥3 unless an explicit q=2 boundary example is given; t≠2 where required.
proofSteps: A quotient of a component by D(q,G) can decrease its degree only by a divisor of |D(q,G)|≤2; retain this factor before canceling.
For even q the torus order n divides q−1 or q+1 and is odd. Thus the remaining possible outer factor 2 cancels from the odd modulus, even for a proper image subgroup.
For odd ℓ this factor and the vertical factor 2 do not affect the valuation.
At t=−2 over an odd prime field use X*=X° and the parabolic p-divisibility.
The larger move-group orbits are unions of orientation-preserving trace orbits, so divisibility survives; do not claim the two groups coincide.
acceptance: The odd-q torus orbit modulus has 4 where the unquotiented component modulus has 2.
For p=5 all orientation-preserving orbits on the 40-point punctured surface must have sizes divisible by 5.
The generalized odd-ℓ congruence is exported to ArithmeticDynamicsPartII, rather than imported from a proof which already uses it.

nodes.title: The split and nonsplit conic fibres
nodes.statement: Let q be odd and t≠2. At a=±2, the full conic C_1(a)_t is empty if t−2 is nonsquare and otherwise is two parallel lines, with 2q points. For distinct split roots of X²−aX+1 it has q−1 points if a²≠t+2, and 2q−1 points, two intersecting lines, if a²=t+2. For irreducible X²−aX+1 it has q+1 points if a²≠t+2, and exactly the single point (a,0,0) if a²=t+2. For even q and t≠0, C_1(0)_t has q points and its rotation orbits have size 2. These statements concern the full conic; X_t* additionally removes every point with fewer than two nonzero coordinates.
hypotheses: q=p^f≥3 unless an explicit q=2 boundary example is given; t≠2 where required.
proofSteps: For repeated roots, complete the square in y∓z and use t−2≠0.
For split distinct roots, factor the quadratic into two independent linear forms; the fibre is a nonzero product equation or the union of its axes.
For nonsplit distinct roots, identify the quadratic with a scalar multiple of the norm F_{q²}→F_q. A nonzero norm fibre has q+1 elements, whereas norm zero has only the zero vector.
In characteristic 2, the square map of F_q is bijective; y+z is fixed to a nonzero value and swapping the coordinates has no fixed point.
acceptance: The nonsplit degenerate full fibre is a singleton, and its X_t* subset is empty.
A split degenerate full fibre has 2q−1 points before removing its intersection or coordinate-axis exclusions.

nodes.title: Markoff components and Higman classes
nodes.statement: Let p≥5 be prime. Assume the group generated by Vieta moves and coordinate permutations, without adjoining even sign changes, is transitive on the punctured coefficient-one Markoff surface over F_p (input G-DYNAMICS). Then Aut^+(F2) is already transitive: an orientation-reversing coordinate transposition fixes the point (3,3,3), so the stabilizer meets both orientation cosets. The stack M(SL2(F_p))_{−2} has precisely two geometric connected components, distinguished by the two noncentral trace −2 Higman classes; the diagonal outer involution exchanges them. Each coarse component is isomorphic to the coarse absolute-level curve M_p and has j-degree D=p(p+3) for p≡1 mod4 and p(p−3) for p≡3 mod4. Its compactification is a smooth proper geometrically connected curve.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Import the finite-field transitivity and point count from the lower combinatorial part of G-DYNAMICS, with the cross-stage ordering stated in that contract.

Use the Vieta/permutation group specified in G-DYNAMICS, without extra sign generators. The coordinate transposition fixing (3,3,3), an actual punctured point for p≥5, meets the reversing coset, so the orientation subgroup is transitive.
Separate the two SL2 Higman classes and the free diagonal outer interchange; an orbit on the quotient meets each class in exactly one exterior-pair orbit.
Use the existing smooth proper compactification and the trace/coarse correspondence.
acceptance: The hypothesis is finite-field transitivity, not transitivity of the positive integer Markoff tree.
The fixed-point argument uses one orientation-reversing element, not the false claim that every group generator fixes (3,3,3).

nodes.title: Markoff branch and cusp counts
nodes.statement: Under the preceding transitivity hypothesis, put D=p(p+3) or p(p−3) as above. The fibre of the compactified M_p over 0 has (D+2)/3 points: exactly one fixed trace triple (3,3,6) and all other γ0-cycles have length 3. The fibre over 1728 has (D+f_p)/2 points, where f_p=2 for p≡1,7 mod8 and f_p=0 for p≡3,5 mod8. The cusp count is the supplied rotation-orbit count C_p=(p−1)Φ(p−1)/2+(p+1)Φ(p+1)/2+κ_p, with κ_p=(−5p+11)/4 if p≡1 mod4 and (−7p−1)/4 otherwise, and Φ(n)=Σ_{d|n}φ(d)/d. The definition of Φ and the finite-field point/rotation counts belong to ArithmeticDynamicsPartII (routed items 85–86), not a second theory here.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Import Φ, |X*(p)| and the rotation-orbit count through G-DYNAMICS.
Solve the γ0 and γ1728 fixed-point equations using the explicit trace formulas; γ0 has order 3 and γ1728 has order 2 on the trace locus.
Translate rotation cycles to cusps by the trace/moduli correspondence; this is a geometric comparison, not a new plan for the combinatorial orbit counts.
acceptance: At p=5, D=40, the branch fibre counts are 14 and 20 and the cusp count is 8.
At p=7, D=28, the branch fibre counts are 10 and 15 and the cusp count is 5.
Replacing (D+2)/3 by (D+1)/3 would miss the correction for the one fixed point.

nodes.title: The genus formula
nodes.statement: Assume p≥5 prime satisfies the transitivity input. Then the common genus of the two compactified trace −2 components equals p²/12−(p−1)Φ(p−1)/4−(p+1)Φ(p+1)/4+ε_p, with ε_p respectively 7p/8−29/24,5p/8+19/24,7p/8−17/24,5p/8+7/24 when p≡1,3,5,7 mod8. It is 0,0,1 for p=5,7,11 and is at least 2 for every p≥13 satisfying the hypothesis. The latter bound uses the explicit lower estimate p²/12−(p−1)^(3/2)/2−(p+1)^(3/2)/2+p/2 and a certified finite check for the remaining primes.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Apply the imported tame Riemann–Hurwitz theorem to the smooth proper connected coarse curve with its three branch fibres.
Equivalently identify its connected branch permutation triple, with σ∞σ1σ0=1, and use its Euler/genus relation.
Substitute D, the two elliptic branch counts and C_p and simplify by p mod8.

Bound Φ(n) by 2sqrt(n), establish positivity beyond an explicit cutoff, and evaluate the finitely many smaller primes exactly; the finite check is part of acceptance, not an unspecified numerical claim.

For 13≤p<2304, exact rational evaluation at all 337 primes gives minimum genus 5 at p=13. For p≥2304, use (p±1)^(3/2)≤(2p)^(3/2)<3p^(3/2) and sqrt(p)≥48 to bound the displayed lower estimate below by p^(3/2)+p/2>2. This supplies a finite, reproducible arithmetic acceptance calculation, not a transitivity proof.
acceptance: The exact formula gives g5=0,g7=0,g11=1,g13=5.
The genus is computed from a connected permutation triple; applying one connected genus identity to a disconnected union of components would be invalid.

nodes.title: Finiteness of elliptic j-invariants
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and p≥13 a prime satisfying the transitivity hypothesis and the verified genus≥2 bound. There are only finitely many geometric elliptic-curve isomorphism classes, equivalently j-invariants in K, admitting a K-rational point on either trace −2 level component; in particular this holds for elliptic curves over K carrying a geometrically connected SL2(F_p)-torsor on E\O with that trace invariant. Apply Faltings after a finite extension over which the geometric components are defined. Do not conclude finiteness of K-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves: quadratic twists preserve j and can produce infinitely many such classes.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Extend K finitely so each relevant smooth proper genus≥2 component is defined and geometrically connected.
Apply the imported Mordell–Faltings theorem to its rational points.
Map the finite set of level points to the j-line and descend the finite set of j-invariants; the implication from an actual torsor to a sheaf level point is sufficient.
acceptance: A finite set of j-invariants is equivalent to finitely many isomorphism classes over an algebraic closure.
The proof must not count all quadratic twists as one K-isomorphism class.

nodes.title: The projective absolute-level quotient
nodes.statement: For p≥5, central twists by Hom(F2,{±I}) give the Klein four action (x,y,z)↦(ε1 x,ε2 y,ε1ε2 z) on X*(p). This is the even sign-change action already owned by CA.4. It is free on the punctured t=−2 locus: a nontrivial fixed sign change forces two zero coordinates and then the third to be zero. The resulting quotient is the finite trace fibre for absolute PSL2(F_p)-structures. Under transitivity its associated coarse component has degree d_p=D/4 and is the curve N_p used for the monodromy statement.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Use the existing even sign action; identify it with central twists of rank-two representations.
Prove freeness on X*(p) by the fixed-coordinate equations.
Compare lifts of projective representations and quotient by projective outer automorphisms, using the full SL2 trace fibre and the two Higman classes.
acceptance: At p=5, D=40 and d_p=10.
At p=7, D=28 and d_p=7.
The origin is fixed by the entire sign group and must be removed before dividing the cardinality by 4.

nodes.title: Large projective monodromy
nodes.statement: Let P_MP be the density-one set of primes p≥5 specified by Meiri–Puder and Chen: p is outside the finite exceptional set E_bgs, and either p≡1 mod4 or p≡3 mod4 with the order of (3+sqrt(5))/2 in F_{p²}^× at least 32sqrt(p+1), interpreted after choosing a root in F_{p²}. For p∈P_MP the geometric monodromy of N_p→P¹_j is S_{d_p} when p≡5,7,9,11 mod16 and A_{d_p} when p≡1,3,13,15 mod16. Its proof requires the independent large-alternating permutation theorem and density result from ArithmeticDynamicsPartII, recorded in G-DYNAMICS, together with the orbit congruence supplied here. The residue classification is a parity computation for the projective branch permutations.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Import the large alternating subgroup theorem, its exact prime set and density-one conclusion from G-DYNAMICS.

The orientation-preserving subgroup has normal image of index at most two in the full permutation image on the even-sign quotient. Since the latter contains A_{d_p}, d_p≥7, and A_{d_p} has no nontrivial quotient of order two, its intersection with the orientation image is all of A_{d_p}. Transfer this image to the geometric fibre.
Compute the signs of the projective γ0 and γ1728 permutations to decide A versus S in each mod16 class.
acceptance: At p=5 the projective degree is 10 and the stated residue class predicts S10.
At p=7 the projective degree is 7 and the stated residue class predicts S7.
The large permutation theorem is an explicit input, not a consequence of knowing only that a group acts transitively.

nodes.title: Noncongruence of Markoff levels
nodes.statement: For p∈P_MP, the finite-index subgroup of SL2(Z) associated to either trace −2 SL2(F_p) component is noncongruence: it contains no principal congruence subgroup. The same obstruction is visible already on the projective absolute quotient N_p, whose monodromy has A_{d_p} as a composition factor with d_p≥7. The only nonabelian simple composition factors of any congruence quotient SL2(Z/n) are PSL2(F_ℓ), and none is isomorphic to A_{d_p} for these d_p≥7. The congruence-subgroup predicate and principal subgroups already exist in Mathlib and are imported unchanged. The composition-factor extension of the existing modular-level quotient theory is requested in Q-CONGRUENCE.
hypotheses: p≥5 prime; characteristic-zero moduli geometry; transitivity and MP inputs only where explicitly assumed.
proofSteps: Use Mathlib CongruenceSubgroup.IsCongruenceSubgroup, and import only the reduction-quotient composition-factor theorem through Q-CONGRUENCE.
If the subgroup were congruence, its permutation monodromy and every quotient would factor through SL2(Z/n).

Use the pinned simplicity of A_d for d≥5. If A_d were PSL2(F_ℓ) with prime ℓ≥5, equality of orders would imply d!=ℓ(ℓ²−1). Since ℓ divides d!, it is at most d; but d!>d³ for d≥7, a contradiction. This avoids invoking an unproved general classification of accidental isomorphisms.
Conclude for the larger SL2 level cover because its projective monodromy is already a quotient.
acceptance: At p=7, A7 is not PSL2(F_ℓ) for any prime ℓ; the accidental A5≅PSL2(F5) does not apply.
A subgroup being nonnormal does not avoid the obstruction: use the permutation action on its cosets, not a group quotient by that subgroup.
